author: Septemberlemon
title: I can't open powertoys settings by double clicking

status.label: Duplicate investigation
status.detail: The detailed Windows 10 Settings-launch evidence is already linked to the open issue #49011; keep it with the shared UI-launch investigation rather than creating a competing fix.

next_action.label: Continue in linked Settings-launch issue
next_action.reason: The reporter linked this report to #49011, which remains open and tracks the matching Windows 10 Settings failure; no additional comment is needed here.

judgment.rationale: The report describes the same Windows 10 Settings window failure tracked by open issue #49011; the reporter already cross-linked this issue there. The detailed CET/runtime evidence and another user's matching mitigation are useful context for that shared investigation. A maintainer's latest reply says the solution may be referenced if the issue returns, but does not establish a PowerToys code fix, so do not claim the underlying problem is fixed or draft another duplicate comment.
evidence: The body reports Settings failing to open on Windows 10 after installing 0.101.2432.0, while it opens on Windows 11.

The reporter's comment identifies Event Viewer exception 0x80131506 in KERNELBASE.dll, says disabling Hardware-enforced Stack Protection or updating Windows restores launch, and reports failure before PowerToys logs are written.
A second commenter confirmed the same workaround pattern for FancyZonesEditor.exe.
The reporter directly linked #50335 from open issue #49011, titled PowerToys Settings window can't open in Windows10; open #40234 separately tracks the broader Windows 10 PowerToys UI launch family.
The latest comment from ssssamstrup thanks the reporter and says the solution will be referenced if the issue returns; no linked fix PR or close event exists.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep this report's CET evidence attached to the existing #49011/#40234 investigations; do not start or post a competing implementation proposal.

fix_assessment.rationale: A separate fix for this duplicate report is not applicable while the matching Windows 10 Settings/UI-launch investigations remain open and already contain the reporter's cross-link; no code fix is established.

inferences: The CET/runtime explanation is plausible from the reported crash and workaround but has not been established as a PowerToys code defect.
Consolidating implementation work under #49011 reduces duplicate effort; the maintainer's latest comment does not confirm that a fix has shipped.
